standard.title: Respectful relationships
standard.description: identify and explore skills and strategies to develop respectful relationships
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have practised personal and social skills to interact respectfully with others (AC9HPFP02). They can demonstrate basic respectful interaction in familiar contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify and explore skills and strategies to develop respectful relationships.

nodes.label: Recognising respectful and disrespectful behaviours
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify behaviours that demonstrate respect and those that may cause hurt, harm or disrespect to others.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one behaviour that demonstrates respect and at least one that causes disrespect or hurt, in a familiar context.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of respectful and disrespectful behaviours across different contexts (stories, physical activities, everyday interactions); distinguish verbal, non-verbal and physical forms of both.
wider: Examine characters in texts who demonstrate respect for different types of families and carers, including those of different cultures, abilities or compositions
Identify and describe verbal and physical forms of bullying and explain how they affect others
Explore what respect looks like for First Nations Australians and how to acknowledge difference using appropriate language
nodes.hinge_reason: Students need a clear conceptual anchor for respectful versus disrespectful behaviour before they can identify or practise strategies to build respect (Node 2). Without this, strategy exploration is superficial — students know what to do but not why.

response_modes.reason: Use stories, role play or movement scenarios to prompt students to name specific behaviours and classify them. Concrete examples from familiar contexts are more effective than abstract definitions at this year band.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one behaviour that shows respect
Identifies at least one behaviour that may cause hurt or disrespect to others

nodes.label: Skills and strategies for respectful relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explore skills and strategies to develop respectful relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one skill or strategy used to show respect in a relationship context and describe how it works.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explore a range of skills and strategies for showing respect in relationships — including appropriate language, body language, inclusion, and encouragement — across different social and movement contexts.
wider: Demonstrate appropriate verbal and non-verbal language (including gestures) when encouraging and including others in physical activities
Explore strategies for showing respect to First Nations Australians and discussing difference using appropriate language
Compare how strategies for showing respect might look different in physical activity contexts versus classroom or social contexts

response_modes.reason: Students benefit from building a repertoire of specific respect strategies across contexts — not just knowing that 'respect is important' but having named, practisable moves they can call on.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Strategies for respectful relationships look different across physical activity, cultural and interpersonal contexts. Students who have explored respect strategies in diverse settings develop a broader and more flexible repertoire than those who have only practised in one context.
success_criteria: Names at least one skill or strategy for showing respect in a relationship
Describes how that skill or strategy contributes to a respectful relationship
